title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Lenses — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State the lens maker's formula and derive it for a thin convex lens.
questions.solution:
**Lens maker's formula:** 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂).

Refraction at the first surface forms an intermediate image; that acts as the object for the second surface. Applying n₁/v − n₂/u = (n₁ − n₂)/R at each surface with the thin-lens sign convention and adding eliminates the intermediate distance, leaving **1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂)**.
questions.knowledgeNote: For equi-convex (R₂ = −R₁ = −R): 1/f = 2(n − 1)/R — the one-line special case NEB loves.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the image distance and magnification.
questions.solution:
1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 → v = **60 cm** (real, on the far side).

m = v/u = 60/30 = **−2**: inverted and twice as large. (Beyond 2F gives a diminished image; between F and 2F, magnified.)
questions.knowledgeNote: Lens m = v/u carries no minus unlike mirrors — sign slips here flip 'erect' and 'inverted'.

questions.question: A convex lens has surfaces of radii 20 cm and −20 cm and n = 1.5. Calculate its focal length using the lens maker's formula.
questions.knowledgeNote: R₂ is negative for double-convex in Cartesian convention — the sign is where this numerical is won or lost.

questions.question: Two thin lenses of powers +5 D and −2 D are placed in contact. Find the power and focal length of the combination.
questions.solution:
Powers add in contact: P = +5 + (−2) = **+3 D** (net converging).

f = 100/P = 100/3 ≈ **33.3 cm**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Spectacle prescriptions are just this arithmetic — plus for hypermetropia, minus for myopia.

questions.question: What are myopia and hypermetropia? Which lenses correct them?
questions.solution:
**Myopia (near-sight):** eyeball too long — distant images focus in front of the retina. Corrected with a **concave (diverging)** lens.

**Hypermetropia (far-sight):** eyeball too short — near images focus behind the retina. Corrected with a **convex (converging)** lens.
questions.knowledgeNote: 'Minus for myopia, plus for hypermetropia' — the alliteration is the memory hook.

questions.question: What is a simple microscope? Write its magnifying power when the image forms at the near point.
questions.solution:
A simple microscope is a single short-focus convex lens used as a magnifier, with the object just inside F.

With the image at the near point D: m = **1 + D/f** (≈ D/f for relaxed-eye viewing at infinity).
questions.knowledgeNote: Shorter f → stronger loupe — watchmakers use ~2 cm lenses for ~13× magnification.
